title: Biased bounded-error decision by a machine
statement: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ decides a Boolean language $L$ within time $T$ with bias $\rho$ if, for every Boolean input string $x$, it halts within $T(|x|)$ steps and outputs the indicator of whether $x\in L$ with biased probability at least $2/3$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$L$ is a language over the Boolean alphabet
$T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
For every Boolean input $x$, $N$ halts within $T(|x|)$ steps
For every Boolean input $x$, the probability of outputting the membership indicator of $x$ in $L$ is at least $2/3$
